sentences.text: Sinovenator is a genus of troodontid dinosaur from China, a group of small, graceful maniraptorans that closely resemble birds, though Sinovenator itself is considered one of the larger troodontid species in the Yixian Formation ecosystem.
A distinguishing feature of this species is that the front edge of the antorbital fenestra, an opening in the skull, is straight and oriented vertically.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated that an individual one meter long weighed 2.5 kilograms.
Hundreds of undescribed fossils of this species are known from the Lujiatun Beds, suggesting it was very common in that specific area.
The remains are notable for being preserved in three dimensions rather than being strongly compressed on a flat slab.
The researchers found the specimens represented a new taxon named Sinovenator, a generic name derived from the Latin word Sinae for China and Venator, meaning hunter.
The species name changii honors Meemann Chang for her significant work on the Jehol Fauna.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific example the species is based on, is cataloged as IVPP V 12615 and consists of a partial skull and a disarticulated skeleton.
As troodontids, Sinovenator possessed sickle-shaped claws, raptorial hands, and high non-avian encephalization quotients indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
Although the holotype and paratype are subadults, larger specimens exist that are about twice their length.
The lack of a bulla on the underside of the braincase is a basal character of Sinovenator.
Sinovenator was classified in the family Troodontidae in 2002.
A 2017 study by Shen et al. placed Sinovenator in a monophyletic group called Sinovenatorinae with other troodontids from the Yixian Formation.
However, a 2018 study by Yin et al. suggested that Chinese troodontids, including Sinovenator, form an intermediate grade rather than a distinct subfamily.

Sinovenator lived during the Early Cretaceous Period, approximately 125 million years ago during the Aptian stage, though other research places its range from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago across the Barremian to Aptian stages.
Four fossil occurrences of Sinovenator have been recorded to date.
There was a debate regarding the age of Sinovenator fossils, originally thought to be Hauterivian but later research indicated they are younger.
